## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

**Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 87** (*Itthālaṅkāra*, "Wearing jewelry") is an offense of expiation belonging to the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Vinaya Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The rule establishes that a Buddhist nun who wears ornaments or personal jewelry incurs a *pācittiya* offense requiring confession [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule has been completed by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral]. Although several secondary Vinaya discussions cite a "Pācittiya 87," these references invariably concern the distinct rule on the permissible height of beds and couches found in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga rather than this nun-specific regulation.

The rule against wearing ornaments is widely shared across early Buddhist Vinaya traditions. SuttaCentral identifies resembling parallels in the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga lineages of the Dharmaguptaka (Lzh Dg Bi Vb Pc 157; lzh-dg-bi-pm-pc157), Mahīśāsaka (Lzh Mi Bi Vb Pc155, Pc156, Pc158; lzh-mi-bi-pm-pc155, pc156, pc158), Sarvāstivāda (Lzh Sarv Bi Vb Pc147; lzh-sarv-bi-pm-pc147, lzh-sarv-bi-pm-dh-pc148), and Mūlasarvāstivāda in both Chinese and Tibetan versions (xct-mu-bi-pm-pc126, xct-mu-bi-vb-pc126, Lzh Mu Bi Vb Pc 180, lzh-mu-bi-pm-pc180), alongside the Pali Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha and Parivāra (Pācittiya 87) [SuttaCentral]. In DharmaNexus, the text exhibits Pali-internal formulaic reuse across 83 texts (231 matching passages), sharing its closest structural and phraseological matches with adjacent Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga rules—especially Pācittiyas 88, 89, 90, 2, and 43—as well as the Bhikkhunikkhandhaka (Kd 20) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns the text cross-linguistically with the Tibetan *Bhikṣuṇīvinayavibhaṅga* (D0005) [DharmaNexus], in agreement with SuttaCentral's Mūlasarvāstivāda parallel [SuttaCentral].
